note: Radiocarbon laboratory codes. A date's laboratory ID is the lab's prefix, a separator and the lab's own sample number (OxA-1234, Beta-456789). Read 2026-11-16 from the Laboratory Code Designations list on radiocarbon.org/laboratories (the journal Radiocarbon, University of Arizona; the downloadable list Labs-2026_08_24.pdf, last updated 24 August 2026). The journal states that lab codes are self-reported and are neither assigned nor regulated by Radiocarbon, and marks with an asterisk the labs reported closed, no longer measuring 14C, or operating under a different code; those carry status 'closed or renamed' here. Names and countries are as the list gives them, with three rows the column layout splits wrongly fixed by hand: NRICH (its name wraps), QU (its country sits inside the name) and the combined row 'GdA, GdS' (two entries); 'Ki (KIEV)' is prefix Ki with alias KIEV. Prefixes are case-sensitive (TKA and TKa, Lu and LU are different labs), and P is listed twice.
